context:
Write a standalone Python script (no external dependencies beyond stdlib)
that uses xml.etree.ElementTree to parse coverage.xml. Group files by
their first two path components (e.g., benchbox/cli, benchbox/core/tpch).
Print a table of packages with coverage, highlight failures, exit 1 if
any package is below threshold. Make threshold configurable via CLI arg.
description:
Once all modules reach ≥50% coverage (via the companion TODO items),
add CI enforcement to prevent regressions below the floor.

Current CI uses --cov-fail-under=50 which checks OVERALL coverage only.
This allows individual modules to drop to 0% as long as the aggregate
stays above 50%. A per-module check would catch this.

Options:
  1. Use coverage.py's [report] fail_under per-package (limited granularity)
  2. Add a custom script that parses coverage.xml and fails on any module <50%
  3. Use diff-cover to enforce coverage on changed files only

Recommend option 2: a lightweight Python script in scripts/ that parses
coverage.xml, groups by top-level package, and fails if any package is
below threshold.

anti_patterns.dont: add external dependencies to the coverage script
anti_patterns.why: it runs in CI where install time matters

anti_patterns.dont: make the script fail on missing coverage.xml
anti_patterns.instead: exit 0 with a warning if the file is absent
anti_patterns.why: not all CI runs generate it

preserves.behavior: Existing passing CI jobs remain passing with no increase in runtime >20%
ci-test Makefile target continues to run pytest with existing flags and pass

verifications.command: uv run -- python scripts/check_module_coverage.py --coverage-xml coverage.xml --threshold 50 --exclude-module benchbox/data --exclude-module benchbox/examples
verifications.description: Script correctly identifies modules below threshold
verifications.expected: table of per-module coverage with pass/fail indicators

verifications.command: uv run -- python scripts/check_module_coverage.py --coverage-xml coverage.xml --threshold 99 --exclude-module benchbox/data --exclude-module benchbox/examples; echo $?
verifications.description: Script exits non-zero when modules fail
verifications.expected: exit code 1 (since no module is at 99%)
